Probably six or seven, am old though and can't recall for certain. Like you, I started with a single shot .22. But unlike you, I lived on the edge of my grandparents small rural farm, and guns and shooting became my main source of entertainment growing up. It didn't hurt that we kids were pretty much allowed to wander off and get out of Mom's hair, I guess - LOL ... and in those days, even a young boy on a farm with a gun was no big deal. It also didn't hurt that I had an uncle that bought and sold guns as a side gig to make extra cash, and he'd drop off an oddball rifle, shotgun, or pistol with some ammo on many a weekend, and let me have it for a week or so to play with. It gave me lifelong love for the sport, and for firearms in general. I've collected (I have a C&R FFL) throughout my life, and though I'm older now and no longer hunt, or even shoot as much as I once did ... it's still a passion.

So anyway, enough about me - LOL - I think six or seven, depending on the maturity level of the child, is fine. But as always, teach safety first and gradually let them free as they grow into handling the handling firearms responsibly. I have two daughters, and started them out in that general time frame.

agreed on the safety aspect. That was most definitely drilled into my head young.

They understood about guns and they weren't some curiosity that they 'got into' when mom and dad were away, if ya get my drift. We read all the time about kids getting daddy's gun to play with it when they sneak into a parents bedroom or something. When the kids are taught about such things early, there's no novelty ... at least generally speaking ... and though most responsible parents try to safely store firearms, shit happens, and they're less likely to get into trouble.
